Coldtea in action

Every other agentic development environment optimizes how fast you write code

Speed stopped being the problem. The risk moved downstream, into regressions nobody caught and incidents your users report first

Coldtea covers what comes after

Coding agents build. QA agents verify every release. Monitoring agents watch production. One environment for end-to-end software delivery, not five

01/Terminal

## Run coding agents as a team [...] ### We don't make you switch editors

Your terminal shell is resolved automatically and your settings carry over, so everything works right away

### We don't move your code off your machine

Cloud execution exists, but only when you turn it on

### We don't sell you another coding agent

Works with Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and more

FAQ

## Questions we get a lot

Anything else, emailhello@coldtea.ai

Coldtea is an IDE, not a dashboard. It runs on your machine, right next to your repo, using the shell, agents and settings you already have. It is a new kind of agentic development environment: the terminal you work in every day, with testing and production monitoring built around it. [...] Free to get started. The terminal is free forever, agentic testing comes with a generous free tier, and production monitoring is free to try.

A wide range, from Sentry and Datadog to Grafana, New Relic, PostHog and Vercel. If yours is missing, request it from inside the app or emailhello@coldtea.ai. Adding a new provider usually takes us about 24 hours.

It uses your app the way a person would. For mobile, it spins up simulators and loads real builds. For web, it drives your live site, and on every pull request it runs against the preview URL so regressions are caught before they merge. Critical flows can be fully automated for release testing, on web and mobile.

## GitClear

According to GeekWire, GitClear “reviews and summarizes your code, teasing out the fraction of work that has a meaningful impact on the codebase.” It’s another platform that shows trends in software teams based on the data gleaned from the Git commit history. In addition, it offers some key software team metrics.

### Status Without Standups

commit activity browser. code climate alternatives GitClear

The commit activity browser shows the Jira ticket each developer is working on and the amount of progress made. So this eliminates the need to pull in a developer merely to get status updates. [...] Coveralls uses code coverage as the defining metric for ensuring code quality and integrity. In fact, it doesn’t offer much value in terms of software metrics for teams.

LinearB and GitClear are more modern platforms that offer the features of the previous two platforms. Equally, they also come packed with features suited to supercharge software teams by providing actionable insights.

While you’re likely to find advantages in each of the alternatives on this list, LinearB offers the most benefits to support you in scaling your software team.

LinearB helps you get your metrics dashboard set up quickly, allowing you to get started in as little as five minutes. [...] ### Open Source

SonarQube is an open-source project with 5,600 stars on GitHub. It’s actively developed with contributions from over 120 developers. As a result, there’s enough support from the community to help if issues arise.

## Coveralls

Coveralls dashboard

Coveralls helps software teams to deliver code confidently by checking how much of the codebase is tested by the test suites. Consequently, the resulting percentage determines the likelihood of an undetected bug making it to production. It also works with GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and CI/CD platforms like Travis CI.

Some of its features can be seen below.
